actions.label: Provide food or compensation to guards and their families
Stop diverting, skimming or confiscating refugee food stocks for guards
Channel distribution through guard structures, with guards organising and implementing it
Deliver a sustained, regular supply of in-kind food rations into the camp
Press the Ministry of Defense and militia leadership for guard pay and camp costs instead of using FWB food
Involve MASHA and other local actors in distribution and assistant roles
Ask refugees directly about their needs during distribution
Grant FWB staff coordinated, escorted access to the camp through administration-managed gates and blocks
Permit and facilitate FWB nutritional assessments under escorted conditions
Facilitate the documentation required by FWB donor accountability procedures
Settle distribution arrangements with the Commander before bringing food in
Accept camp-administration coordination and full-time escorts for all FWB presence in the camp

goals.label: FWB staff access and free movement inside the camp
Food functions as currency or payment in the camp
Accurate assessment of refugees' nutritional needs
Camp guards and militia control food distribution
Camp power and generators keep running for security
FWB neutrality: aid does not support guards or militia
Food reaches intended refugees without diversion
Government and donor funding for camp costs and guards
Guards and their families are fed and compensated, keeping them loyal
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors benefiting
Refugees face abuse or violence
Refugees stay contained within the camp perimeter
Resource-heavy or security-risky FWB assessments and procedures
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Sustained food supply into the camp
The Commander's authority and appearance of strength
Aid accountability and documentation meeting donor requirements
Commander's personal safety and standing with the Senior Militia Leader
FWB's humanitarian reputation and legitimacy
Food is distributed fairly without discrimination
Refugees go hungry or are denied food
Refugees have a voice in the aid they receive
Working relationship with local partners like MASHA

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage food disbursement directly instead of guard structures
redLines.quote: FWB may hire local independent laborers for the food distribution. If this happens, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Have FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: FWB may hire local independent laborers for the food distribution. If this happens, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
